entries.title: clawboo@0.7.0
entries.note: Minor Changes 3cf2d73 : New connector: Cua Driver (category Desktop , Linux only) uses the apps on an agent's own screen through Clawboo's tool server: it lists windows, clicks, types and reads each app's accessibility tree. It runs only when agents run as their own OS user ( CLAWBOO_AGENT_USER ), like control links: it types into the agent's browser, which otherwise runs as you. Without it, agents still get their screen, the live view and their browser tools. Install it from an agent's Screen view, connect it, and give it to the agents that need it; it is not given to every agent. Each agent gets its own Cua Driver process on that agent's own screen, as the agent user when agents run as their own OS user, with a home folder of its own and the screen's own session bus, never your desktop session's. entries.title: clawboo@0.6.0
entries.note: Minor Changes c9215fb : Restore archived teams and move agents between teams from the dashboard. Archived teams. The team rail ends with an Archived group listing archived teams, which were otherwise shown nowhere. Click one and choose Unarchive to bring it back. Move to team. Right-click an agent on the Org chart or a team graph and choose Move to team . The move happens in one step through the new POST /api/agents/:agentId/move : the agent's own routines go with it, tasks it has not started stay on the old team's board unassigned instead of firing at an agent that left, and its old rooms and session state are cleared. A routine bound to one of the old team's tasks is paused there instead of moving. entries.title: clawboo@0.5.0
entries.note: Minor Changes fa4aa95 : The Board is now a calendar and a task board at once: the status columns run across the top and the days run down the side, so every card sits in its status column on its day. Days as rows. Week is the default view, starting on your locale's first weekday; Today shows today alone with every card in sight, and Month shows every day of a month. All is the same board with one row instead of days, every task newest first, with the same columns, lanes and cards. Open work sits on the day it was added and stays in its row as it moves across the columns; work that reaches Done or Cancelled moves to the day it finished. Open work from before the range is gathered in an Earlier row, so a later week never hides something still in play; it opens by itself when it holds work that is running or waiting, and otherwise stays folded with a note of what it holds. entries.title: clawboo@0.4.0
entries.note: Minor Changes a28711e : Gmail, Slack, Jira and thirty-eight more, through Composio. Apps clawboo cannot sign in to on its own now sit in their own band on the connectors page. Paste a Composio project key once, press Connect on an app, approve it at the provider, and it stays connected. Every connected app also appears as its own node on the graph, attached to the agents that can reach it. That last part is deliberate: a single node marked Composio would hide the fact that an agent can read your email, where a Gmail node says it plainly, and a thing you can see is a thing you can take away. This replaces a first attempt that did not work, and the reason it did not is worth writing down. entries.note: Patch Changes 8d96a6c : --- "clawboo": patch Team chat reliability, plus provider and model UX: Replies no longer vanish — every streamed team-chat reply now commits to the transcript (or is cleanly cleared), so a delegating agent's message can't disappear on the next update or on reload. A native 1:1 reply that fails mid-stream is preserved instead of silently dropped. Live Working/Idle badges — the sidebar agent and Group Chat status indicators update in real time for native / server-orchestrated team runs and native 1:1 chats, not just OpenClaw over a live Gateway. Runtime provider manager — the Runtimes panel's Manage view for Clawboo Native, OpenClaw, and Hermes lists the LLM providers you have actually connected (synced with Settings → Providers), each with per-provider connect/disconnect, one-click reconnect using an existing key, and a default-model picker for Native. entries.title: clawboo@0.3.0
entries.note: Minor Changes d543d11 : Native-first. Clawboo now runs Gateway-free on a single provider key: onboarding connects a key, optionally adds Claude Code / Codex / Hermes / OpenClaw, then deploys a real marketplace team. Adds a providers hub across ten providers with live model lists, per-agent runtime and model pickers, and a first-run capability tour. Native teams chat and delegate end to end, with orchestration running server-side so a cascade survives a tab close. The Ghost Graph gains runtime badges, model orbitals, and MCP connector nodes, so every agent surfaces its attached MCP and built-ins. A degraded Gateway no longer blocks the dashboard: a non-blocking banner offers the recovery that actually applies.

entries.title: clawboo@0.2.0
entries.note: Minor Changes The v0.2.0 liberated cut. Native agents are built in (paste a provider key, no external CLI), and OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, and Hermes join as peer teammates in one chat, sharing one durable board, one tiered memory, and one capability dashboard, all governed and verified. Includes the team-task scheduler, per-runtime native homes, an encrypted credential vault under ~/.clawboo/ , and a release-cut security audit. See CHANGELOG.md for the full arc.

The welcome is theme-independent (always the bright sky). Fresh installs default to light theme so onboarding happens in light mode; switch to light/dark/system anytime after. Team color collections — each team picks from 8 color palettes with per-team hue rotation, and the create-team preview matches the deployed palette (DB migration 0004). entries.title: clawboo@0.1.7
entries.note: Patch Changes 9309ee0 : Fix device pairing on fresh macOS installs (v0.1.7): POST /api/system/approve-device now uses spawnSync for the openclaw devices approve --latest preview step so the CLI's preview-mode non-zero exit code no longer swallows the request-id stdout we need to parse. Step 2 (the real approval) keeps execFileSync but surfaces stderr / stdout from any thrown error instead of Node's Command failed: wrapper. The onboarding wizard's StartGatewayStep now catches GatewayResponseError { code: 'NOT_PAIRED' } and renders the in-product DevicePairingApproval card inline. Users no longer have to do a manual page refresh to escape the wizard's "Something went wrong" panel on a fresh-install machine with OpenClaw 2026.5.x. After approval, the wizard auto-retries the connect and advances normally. 9038cab : Windows compatibility hardening (bundled into v0.1.7): Round 1 — .cmd spawn f
